newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gencor might consider future debt issues.
newsitem.headline: Gencor might consider future debt issues.

text.p: Low gearing levels at South African mining house Gencor Ltd and its planned British base metals unit Billiton Plc might see it tapping international debt markets in future, chairman Brian Gilbertson said on Wednesday.
"Yes I think it's possible," Gilbertson told Reuters when asked if the company might approach the debt markets in future.
"Billiton will have a very low level of gearing...and I think it will be able to gear itself more," he said.
But there were no immediate plans to raise debt capital, Gilbertson added.
His comments came after Gencor's announcement that it planned to list base metals group Billiton in London and raise $1 billion in an international equity placement.

"Coming out of the (Billiton) capital raising we'll be in a very strong financial position and I think we'll make a judgment then. I believe the capital we're raising now will see us through our planning period of three to five years."

Gilbertson said Gencor, which had a gearing ratio of about 20 percent at the end of 1996, was no stranger to debt markets, unlike most South African companies which favoured equity as a source of project finance.
Gencor used debt capital to finance its 466,000 tonne Hillside Aluminium smelter in Richards Bay, commissioned last year.

Gilbertson noted the capital reduction planned as part of the recently announced merger of Australia's QNI Ltd and Gencor's nickel assets was designed to reap benefits from a higher gearing level for the Australian firm.
